text:
The New York Post calls it a "grind game" fueling the Rangers' new identity, and our numbers agree that J.T. Miller is driving play. At 33, back in New York, he plays 19 minutes a night and the Rangers take 62% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) when he's out at even strength, 14.31 points better than when he sits.

The scoreboard hasn't caught up. Miller has five goals on 8.37 expected, and the Rangers have scored 10 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That gap is the kind that tends to close, and it's why 19 points in 24 games undersells him. Evolving-Hockey saw the same pattern last season: 0.9 expected wins against -0.2 actual. Our numbers project 65 points. If the finishing around him turns ordinary, the points should follow the chances.
headline: J.T. Miller is creating more than the scoreboard shows
